title: “Most nearly mean” in a literary excerpt
subtitle: Words in Context · 40 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **40 of the official questions in Words in Context are this one** — 32 Easy, 4 Medium, 4 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The prompt names a word or short phrase in quotation marks and asks what it most nearly means as used in the text.
- The passage is usually an adapted poem or older prose, often with an introduction naming the author and date.
- The choices are single words or short phrases that could all be dictionary meanings of the word.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Cover the choices, reread the line that contains the word, and put in a plain word of your own that fits the image or comparison around it.
- 2) Pick the choice that matches your word, then put it back into the line to confirm it keeps the meaning of the sentence.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick the word's most common meaning, or a meaning suggested by how it looks or sounds, when the poem is using a different or figurative sense.
Another trap is a choice that fits the poem's overall mood but does not mean the same as the word.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
